description:
The knowingly-accepted mint-UI breakage has no tracked remediation story, so the cutover ships an indefinite outage

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): QA under C4: no assets at risk, no code defect, and the availability loss is an informed, documented owner decision that Law 3 places outside the report. The reportable residual is that the remediation is unbounded and tracked only in comments - disclosure and scheduling hygiene. Filed in the QA bundle so it is visible outside a package.json comment; the downgrade from Low is a precision correction, not a suppression.
impact: None. Contracts are correct; direct and multicall callers are unaffected. User-facing mint availability via the UI is lost from the moment of broadcast until an unscheduled follow-up ships.
attackPath: 1. No attacker and no defect. Whitelisting three reward tokens makes `batchMint`'s `minRewards` array length-3, and `getNudgeTokens()` reorders on removal (swap-and-pop), so callers must re-fetch immediately before every call.
2. The `//promotion-ready` annotation and the script both record that 'the live mint UI is BROKEN until a phlimbo-ui story ships a 3-element array plus a getNudgeTokens() re-fetch'.
3. Story line 1447 states: 'The `phlimbo-ui` follow-up story … is **still unraised**. The live mint UI breaks the moment this broadcasts. Tracked as a comment at `story-dependencies.md:218`.'
4. A comment in a dependencies file is not a raised story, so the outage is unbounded in duration rather than sequenced.
recommendation:
Raise the phlimbo-ui story before the Ledger session and sequence it as a same-day follow-up, so the outage window is a known number of hours rather than open-ended. If the cutover must go first, state the expected remediation date in the completion summary. Related: the two-coexisting-batch-minter-ABIs trap (legacy 3-arg on the four per-token minters, 4-arg multi-token on the shared one) belongs in that story's scope explicitly, since a UI that re-fetches `getNudgeTokens()` against a legacy minter will revert - that view does not exist there.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM: cite ledger Q-04 (a807cc7a) in that story's scope so the script-side legacy scalar-`minReward` call sites and the UI-side 3-element-array surface are covered by one follow-up rather than two.
recommendationQuality: strong - a concrete scheduling action plus an explicit scope item for the follow-up story

pocNote: No standalone PoC. Evidence is the run-22 mainnet-fork PREVIEW execution of `promotion-ready:dry` at block 25659373 (see the script-audit review artifacts).

severityDebate.law3Analysis: The outage itself is a KNOWING, documented, priced owner decision with an OBVIOUS consequence - the owner would not be surprised - so under Law 3 it is trusted and is NOT reported as a footgun or a misconfiguration. Applying the surprise test cleanly separates two things the finding bundles: the DECISION (obvious, trusted, out of scope) and the TRACKING (a same-day-or-never outage recorded only inside a package.json comment and a comment at story-dependencies.md:218, which is the thing that can silently persist). Only the second is reportable, and it is disclosure/scheduling hygiene with no code defect - QA. This lands consistently with its class sibling, ledger Q-04 (a807cc7a), which is already `qa` and covers the complementary script-side half of the same cutover break.
severityDebate.notSuppressed: Explicitly NOT closed under the 'reckless admin mistakes' known-invalid rule. Nobody is acting recklessly and nothing is being second-guessed; the item exists to bound the duration and to move the record out of a package.json comment. The sanitizer's candour note - that a reasonable triager could legitimately close this on Law 3 - is preserved so the human decides deliberately rather than inheriting the decision from a filter.

ledgerRelationships.relation: COMPLEMENTARY HALVES OF ONE CUTOVER BREAK, NOT DUPLICATES. Q-04 covers the SCRIPT-side call sites that still bind the legacy scalar-minReward signature and 'silently break on the story-072 cutover'; PR-12 covers the UI-side 3-element-array + getNudgeTokens() re-fetch. Q-04's ledger note already states it is 'OWNER-VISIBLE and explicitly NOT bundled away (Law 2)'. ACTION FOR THE REPORT: PR-12's recommendation (scope the two-coexisting-ABI trap into the phlimbo-ui story) should cite Q-04 so the follow-up story covers both surfaces at once.
